drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you for stopping your review. Defendant asserts attorney-client privilege and work-product protection over the inadvertently included internal material and requests its return or deletion, including copies, subject to any applicable preservation requirement or procedure for resolving a disputed privilege claim. Pending disposition, please sequester it, refrain from using or disclosing it, and take reasonable steps to retrieve any onward disclosures. Please confirm sequestration and advise whether you dispute the claim. If disputed, please maintain sequestration and follow the applicable procedure for determination without public disclosure. Defendant will preserve the material pending resolution and does not intend to waive any protection.

We agree that the general production commitment needs request-specific clarification. The current draft does not establish which requests involve actual withholding, and we will not characterize that status without verification. We propose serving supplemental, request-specific responses within seven calendar days after agreement on this protocol, identifying each maintained objection, its grounds, whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis, and the scope of any withholding.

We propose initial production within 14 calendar days after agreement, rolling productions at least every 14 calendar days thereafter, and substantial completion within 35 calendar days after agreement. Privilege logs would accompany each tranche or follow within 14 calendar days, with a final log due within 14 calendar days after substantial completion. These proposals do not extend any existing deadline absent agreement and any required court approval. Please identify any requested modifications or priority requests.

edits.text: 1. OBJECTIONS AND WITHHOLDING. Defendant asserts attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another applicable protection only where supported by the responsive material and applicable law. No general objection substitutes for a request-specific response. Within seven calendar days after agreement on the proposed protocol, Defendant will serve supplemental responses identifying, for each request, each maintained objection and its specific grounds, whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis, and the scope of any withholding without revealing protected information. For any partial objection, the supplemental response will identify the portion subject to the objection and the portion for which production will proceed.

2. PRODUCTION—PROPOSED SCHEDULE. Defendant proposes to begin producing responsive, nonprivileged documents within 14 calendar days after agreement on this protocol, make rolling productions at intervals not exceeding 14 calendar days, and substantially complete production within 35 calendar days after agreement. Production of undisputed materials will proceed notwithstanding disputes concerning other materials. At substantial completion, Defendant will identify any outstanding production categories and propose specific completion dates. Any extension requires agreement and any required court approval; notice of delay alone does not extend a deadline. This proposal does not displace an existing deadline under applicable rules or court order.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG—PROPOSED PROTOCOL. Unless applicable rules, court order, or agreement provide otherwise, Defendant proposes to provide a log with each production tranche or within 14 calendar days thereafter, and a final log within 14 calendar days after substantial completion. Each entry will include a unique identifier; the associated request number or numbers; date; document type; author and recipients, including copied recipients and their relevant roles where known; a description sufficient to assess the claim without revealing protected information; and the specific protection asserted and basis for the claim. Logged redactions will identify the corresponding produced document. Categorical logging or exclusions from logging will be used only as permitted by applicable rules, court order, or agreement. Defendant will identify any claimed logging exclusion and its authority. The parties will confer within seven calendar days after written notice of a logging deficiency or privilege dispute, without altering any applicable challenge deadline.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will timely supplement or correct its responses, production, and privilege log as required by applicable rules or court order. Supplementation is not a reservation of a unilateral right to defer production or extend agreed or court-ordered deadlines.
